after.decay: The long ship made it out. Most of what it left behind did not.
after.muddle: The long ship is still out there, sending home the kind of news nobody reads.
after.ascent: The long ship arrived somewhere. Its letters home are taught in schools.

after.decay: Something you put in orbit is still up there. Nobody down here can reach it any more.
after.muddle: The station is still up there, kept alive by a budget line nobody dares to cut.
after.ascent: Orbit became ordinary. Children wave at the station the way yours waved at trains.

after.decay: Nobody has voted in living memory. The ballot boxes are in a museum, labelled as pottery.
after.muddle: Elections were suspended and never quite resumed. Every year, someone promises next year.
after.ascent: Nobody voted and it went well anyway, which historians find more upsetting than if it had not.

after.decay: The purge never formally ended. It ran out of people anyone was sure about.
after.muddle: The purge is a chapter in the textbooks, and the chapter is short.
after.ascent: The purge was investigated, named and apologised for, which is more than most countries manage.

after.decay: The general's people still run the checkpoints. They have forgotten what they were checking for.
after.muddle: The army went back to barracks, eventually, and kept the barracks.
after.ascent: The general's statue was moved to a smaller square, which counts here as a reckoning.

decay.right: The House That Ate the State

after.decay: Your heir named an heir. The family still holds the office and none of them want it.
after.muddle: The heir was competent enough. The family tree is on the currency.
after.ascent: The heir you named gave the office back, which is the only thing anyone remembers about them.

after.decay: The oracle is still running. Nobody remembers the question.
after.muddle: The oracle is still consulted, and ignored, in that order.
after.ascent: The oracle's answers are published, and nobody has yet found one that was wrong.

after.decay: Half a ring hangs over the equator. On clear nights you can see where the money ran out.
after.muddle: The ring is three-quarters built, and has been for as long as anyone has been alive.
after.ascent: The ring was finished. You can see it from anywhere, which was the point.

after.decay: The country was asked once. The answer is kept in a drawer, still sealed.
after.muddle: The referendum settled the question for about a generation, which is all they ever do.
after.ascent: Asking the country directly became a habit. It is slow, and it has not been wrong yet.

after.decay: The seawall still stands. Nothing behind it is worth keeping dry.
after.muddle: The seawall held, and the coast behind it is exactly as dull as it was, which is the triumph.
after.ascent: The seawall still stands, and the coast behind it is the most expensive land on the continent.

after.decay: The rationing never lifted. Water is a currency now, and a volatile one.
after.muddle: The rationing ended in the cities and never quite ended anywhere else.
after.ascent: The rationing taught a country to count its water. It still does, and it never runs short.

after.decay: The bridge fell. The two halves of the city stopped speaking, then stopped trading.
after.muddle: The bridge fell and was replaced by a ferry, which was replaced by a slightly larger ferry.
after.ascent: The bridge fell. The one they built instead is on the stamps.

after.decay: The moonshot budget was spent. The rocket was not.
after.muddle: The moonshot programme still exists, as a department, with a canteen.
after.ascent: The moonshot paid for itself in a way nobody predicted and everybody now claims they did.

after.decay: The feed is still run from the office. It has not reported bad news in two hundred years.
after.muddle: The feed is still run from here, and people have learned to read it upside down.
after.ascent: The feed was handed back, eventually, and now it is mostly weather and recipes.

after.decay: The housing still stands. It is the best-built thing in the country, and it is full.
after.muddle: The housing was built and is still lived in, which is more than most promises manage.
after.ascent: The housing was built, then more, then more. Nobody under forty remembers a waiting list.

after.decay: The commission is still sitting. Its members are the grandchildren of its members.
after.muddle: The commission publishes an interim report every decade, on schedule, to nobody.
after.ascent: The commission finally reported. It was right about nearly everything, too late for nearly all of it.

after.decay: The late boxes were never explained. Counting after the close became the way it is done.
after.muddle: The late boxes are still argued about, in the way that settles nothing and changes nothing.
after.ascent: The late boxes were recounted in public and the rules changed. It only had to happen once.

after.decay: The audit is still buried, and so is everything it would have found.
after.muddle: The audit was found decades later and published to general indifference.
after.ascent: The audit was dug up and read aloud. It is the founding document of the modern treasury.

after.decay: You broke the promise you took the job on. Nobody has believed one since.
after.muddle: The promise you broke is a proverb now, used about weather and landlords.
after.ascent: The promise was broken, then kept by whoever came after, which is how most promises are kept.

after.decay: The pensions were spent and never replaced. Nobody here retires; they just stop.
after.muddle: The fund was refilled slowly, and the people it was taken from did not live to see it.
after.ascent: The pensions were repaid with interest, by a generation that decided it owed them.

after.decay: The schools were never fed. The country forgot how to fix things, then how to want to.
after.muddle: The schools recovered, eventually. One generation did not, and it shows in the statistics.
after.ascent: The schools were starved and the children taught each other anyway, which is the story everyone prefers.

after.decay: The press still answers to the office. It has never once been surprised.
after.muddle: The press answers to the office in principle and to its advertisers in practice.
after.ascent: The press was handed back and immediately turned on everyone, which is how you know it worked.

after.decay: The skim became the budget, and the budget became a rumour.
after.muddle: The skim is still taken, at a rate everybody knows and nobody says.
after.ascent: The skim was found, returned and spent on a hospital that carries your name, which is the joke.

after.decay: The inquiry you promised was never held, and the questions stopped being asked.
after.muddle: The inquiry was promised, delayed, promised again, and finally held by a successor who found nothing.
after.ascent: The inquiry you shelved was reopened and finished. It is required reading now.

after.decay: The deficit you promised to close grew until it was the economy.
after.muddle: The deficit is still there, and so is the promise to close it, and so is the laughter.
after.ascent: The deficit was outgrown rather than closed, which economists still argue was cheating.

after.decay: The homes you promised were never built. The lots became car parks, then nothing.
after.muddle: The housing promise became a slogan, and the slogan became a joke about slogans.
after.ascent: The homes you promised were built by someone else, who took the credit, which was fair.

after.decay: The taxes you swore not to raise went up, and kept going, and paid for less every year.
after.muddle: The new rate became the old rate, and nobody remembers the one before that.
after.ascent: The taxes went up and something was built with them, the rarest sentence in the country's history.

after.decay: The cheap win became the only win. Every campaign since has been worse than yours.
after.muddle: The habit of the cheap win outlived you, as habits do, at about the same level.
after.ascent: The cheap wins were written into the rulebook as things you cannot do, with yours as the example.

after.decay: An election was counted twice, and after that every election was a formality.
after.muddle: The election you counted twice is remembered, and it is remembered as normal.
after.ascent: Yours was the last election counted twice. The one after it was watched by everyone.

after.decay: The answer was always the same one, and the question stopped being asked.
after.muddle: The office still reaches for the same answer first, and occasionally it is right.
after.ascent: The clamp was loosened a notch a decade, until nobody could remember it being tight.

after.decay: The rules bent for the same people until the rules were the people.
after.muddle: The rule still bends for the same families, which everyone knows and the forms do not.
after.ascent: The rules were straightened, painfully, and the families involved sued, and lost.

after.decay: Money was taken by habit, then by right, then by everyone.
after.muddle: Money is still taken by habit, in amounts too small to prosecute and too large to ignore.
after.ascent: The habit of taking was broken, slowly, by paying people enough to stop.

after.decay: You left nothing a historian could point at. The country fell anyway, just without a reason.
after.muddle: You left no mark a historian could find, which some of them consider the achievement.
after.ascent: You left nothing to point at and the country rose anyway, which is either the best review or the worst.

ascent.left: The War That Kept Its Word

after.decay: The war for the ally never quite ended. It became the reason for everything else.
after.muddle: The war was won, or at least stopped, and the ally still sends a card every year.
after.ascent: The war was fought in the open and ended in a treaty that still holds. Both countries teach it the same way.

after.decay: The country stayed out and sold to both sides. The ally never forgave it, and neither did the photograph.
after.muddle: The country stayed out of the war. Historians still argue about it, which is the most a neutral can hope for.
after.ascent: The country stayed out, said so plainly, and took in the survivors. The ally's grandchildren are citizens now.

after.decay: The deportations ran without hearings until nobody could say who had been a citizen. The fields went quiet first.
after.muddle: The deportations went through the courts, slowly. The last hearing was held long after anyone remembered the first.
after.ascent: Everyone got a hearing, which took years and cost a fortune. The courts built for it are still the best in the country.

after.decay: The checks simply stopped, and never started again. A generation lived here without a single document saying so.
after.muddle: A way to papers was opened and taken, slowly. Their grandchildren vote, mostly for whoever reminds them.
after.ascent: A way to papers was passed as a law and kept as one. The newcomers' grandchildren run half the country.

after.decay: The top rate was cut and never paid for. The debt it left is older than anyone now paying it.
after.muddle: The top rate was cut. The growth came, a little, and the argument about it never ended.
after.ascent: The cut was paid for in the open, line by line. It is the only tax cut the treasury still uses as an example.

after.decay: The very rich were taxed on paper. The money was spent before it came, and it never came.
after.muddle: The very rich were taxed, and paid about half. Every government since has promised the other half.
after.ascent: The very rich were taxed and the loopholes closed. The rich stayed, to general astonishment.

after.decay: Care was promised free and put on the debt. The list is still there, and the debt, and the promise.
after.muddle: Everyone was covered, eventually, after a wait. The wait is a national institution.
after.ascent: Care was made universal and paid for in the open. Nobody alive has seen a medical bill.

after.decay: Care was left to the insurers, who wrote the rules and left out the expensive towns. The towns are still out.
after.muddle: Care was left to a market with vouchers. It works well for the people it works for.
after.ascent: Care was left to a market with rules that had teeth. It is the one market nobody complains about.

after.decay: The minimum wage was raised by decree and never enforced. The cafés still pay the old one, in cash.
after.muddle: The minimum wage went up and stayed up, a little behind the prices, as it always is.
after.ascent: The minimum wage was raised and enforced, café by café. Nobody here works for less, and the cafés are still open.

long.ascent: The Wage Won at the Table

after.decay: Wages were left to employers and to deals signed over the workers' heads. Some are still paid in vouchers.
after.muddle: Wages were left to the bargaining table, which worked wherever there was a table.
after.ascent: Wages were left to the table, and everyone got a seat at it. The cafés have a union now, and so do the farms.

after.decay: The zoning rules were cleared and the towers went up, empty or cracked. The rents never came down.
after.muddle: The rules were cleared and a great deal was built, some of it for the people who needed it.
after.ascent: The rules were cleared, homes were built first, and every one was inspected. Rents fell, and stayed down.

after.decay: The rents were frozen and the buildings were left to fall. The ones still standing are the ones nobody inspected.
after.muddle: The rents were controlled, the landlords complained, and both are still here.
after.ascent: The rents were controlled and the repairs were paid for. The blocks from that time are still the ones people want.

after.decay: Carbon was priced and the plants shut before anything replaced them. The old still date things from the dark winter.
after.muddle: Carbon was given a price. It went up slowly and the smoke came down slowly, and both are still going.
after.ascent: Carbon was priced and the money went back to the people paying it. The last coal plant is a museum with a café.

after.decay: The valley was drilled without a review. The taps ran brown for a generation, and the gas went to whoever paid most.
after.muddle: The gas under the valley was drilled and burned. The valley is quieter now, and so is the refinery.
after.ascent: The gas was drilled with care and kept for the country's own winters. The valley's water is still clean.

after.decay: Tariffs went up, the owners paid themselves, and the factories closed anyway. The tariffs still protect nothing.
after.muddle: The tariffs saved some factories for a while, and raised the price of everything for longer.
after.ascent: The tariffs were tied to new machines, and the machines came. Some of the factories they saved are still running.

after.decay: Trade was opened on terms written elsewhere. The country was sued for its own laws until it stopped writing them.
after.muddle: Trade was opened. The shoes got cheaper and the factory towns got quieter, and people still argue which mattered more.
after.ascent: Trade was opened with the towns retrained first. The old factory towns make things nobody had heard of then.

after.decay: The pension age was raised overnight and the savings spent the same year. People here retire at whatever age they stop.
after.muddle: The pension age went up two years and stayed there. Everyone grumbled, and then everyone worked them.
after.ascent: The pension age went up slowly and the savings stayed in the fund. It is the only fund of its time still paying.

after.decay: The pension age was kept and paid for by borrowing from the fund. The fund is a building now, and rented.
after.muddle: The pension age was kept, and every government since has promised to change it.
after.ascent: The pension age was kept and paid for in the open, a little more from everyone. It is still where it was.

after.decay: Student debt was cancelled by decree, struck down, and owed twice. That year's graduates say "decree" like a curse.
after.muddle: Student debt was cancelled once, and the next year's students borrowed it all again.
after.ascent: Student debt was cancelled by a law that paid for it. The universities have been free ever since.

after.decay: Student debt was sold to collectors, who took it from wages. A generation of nurses paid theirs off abroad.
after.muddle: Student debt was left to be repaid, and it was, slowly, by people who remember every payment.
after.ascent: Student debt stayed with the state and was collected fairly. It is the only loan anyone here speaks of kindly.

after.decay: Drugs were cracked down on until the police sold what they seized. The corner by the school has a dealer in uniform.
after.muddle: The crackdown filled the prisons and emptied some corners. The rest moved two streets over.
after.ascent: The crackdown went through the courts, warrant by warrant. It took years, and the corners stayed clear.

after.decay: Drugs were legalised and the gangs were licensed to sell them. The gangs are still licensed, and own the ports.
after.muddle: Drugs were legalised and taxed. Fewer went to prison, more went to the doctor, and the argument never ended.
after.ascent: Drugs were legalised, taxed and sold plainly, by people who had never been dealers. The prisons have spare rooms.

after.decay: More police went out untrained, and the prisons were paid by the bed. The beds are still full.
after.muddle: There were more police and longer sentences. The streets got a little safer and the prisons a lot fuller.
after.ascent: The new police were trained for two years, and it showed. The prisons were built by the state, and are half empty.

after.decay: The prisons were emptied too fast and the police were left to watch themselves. Neither was ever quite fixed.
after.muddle: The prisons were reformed, slowly, and the police were watched, sometimes.
after.ascent: The prisons were reformed with somewhere to go afterwards. Most who left never came back, which was the point.

after.decay: Every face on every street was scanned and kept. The lists are still kept, by people nobody elected.
after.muddle: The scanners went up and stayed. People stopped noticing them, which was what the scanners wanted.
after.ascent: The scanners searched only with a warrant and forgot every face after a day. The muggings stopped anyway.

after.decay: Face scanners were banned, except the ones nobody banned. Those are still running, and still unofficial.
after.muddle: The scanners were banned. The muggings went on, and so did the argument.
after.ascent: The scanners were banned, all of them, the police's included. Nobody here has had their face counted since.

after.decay: A law decided what was true, and the ministry decided the law. Nobody believes anything official now, even the weather.
after.muddle: A law against misinformation was passed. It caught some lies and some jokes, and was argued about forever.
after.ascent: An independent panel decided what was false, and was usually right. Lying in public is still rare here, and expensive.

after.decay: No law decided what was true, so nothing was. Half the country still believes something made up in an afternoon.
after.muddle: There was no law against lies, and there were a great many lies. The truth did about as well as usual.
after.ascent: No law was passed. The lies were answered with facts, every time, until answering became a habit.

after.decay: Seats were added to the highest court, then more, then more. It is bigger than the parliament, and meets more often.
after.muddle: Four seats were added to the highest court. The next government added four more, and there it stopped, for now.
after.ascent: Four seats were added and filled from the bar's own list. Both sides trust the court, which neither side admits.

after.decay: The court was left alone, and then ignored. Its rulings are still printed, and still not read.
after.muddle: The highest court was left alone. It struck some things down and kept others, as courts do.
after.ascent: The court was left alone and obeyed, even when it ruled against the government. Especially then.

after.decay: The banks were rescued, and the rescue went on bonuses and dividends. They have been rescued twice since.
after.muddle: The banks were rescued. They are still there, a little smaller, and still asking.
after.ascent: The banks were rescued on conditions and paid back every coin. The public seat on each board is still filled.

after.decay: The banks were allowed to fail with the savers inside. People here keep their money under the floor, and say why.
after.muddle: The banks failed. The bankers lost everything, and so did some people who were not bankers.
after.ascent: The banks were allowed to fail, and every small saver was paid. It is the only crash anyone remembers fondly.

after.decay: The census was never honest again. The country knows its own size to within a few million, depending on who asks.
after.muddle: The adjusted count stood for a generation, and the suburbs were under-represented, politely, for the whole of it.
after.ascent: The next census found the adjustment and counted everyone, and every census since has counted twice to be sure.

long.decay: The Age of the Empty Stands

after.decay: The stadium was still being paid for when it fell down. Its ruins host a market on Sundays.
after.muddle: The stadium cost too much and was used too little, and it became the place the country went to argue about both.
after.ascent: The stadium was opened to everyone and filled every weekend for a century. The debt was paid off in its fortieth year.

after.decay: The currency never recovered. People keep their savings in tinned food, and trade the labels.
after.muddle: The money was replaced twice and trusted once, and the old notes paper a museum of bad decisions.
after.ascent: The printing was stopped in time, and the country has distrusted a printing press ever since, usefully.

after.decay: The code was enforced on paper long after the inspectors stopped visiting. The buildings know the difference.
after.muddle: The code outlasted the scandal that brought it in, and the schools stayed up through two earthquakes.
after.ascent: The code became a point of pride. The next great earthquake knocked down a museum of old ones, and nothing else.

long.muddle: The Age of the Large Hat

after.decay: The crown came back as a symbol and stayed as a government. The republic is a chapter in its history books.
after.muddle: The crown stayed ceremonial, mostly. Every few years it tries to appoint someone, and every few years it is told no.
after.ascent: The crown settled into opening bakeries and cutting ribbons, and the republic ran happily around it.

after.decay: The levee held while everything around it failed. The valley is the one dry place in a country that forgot to maintain the rest.
after.muddle: The levee held every spring, and the engineers who tested it are the only officials the valley still trusts.
after.ascent: The levee held for a century, and the week of tests before the ribbon became the country's idea of doing things properly.

long.muddle: The Age of the Price List

after.decay: Every title in the country has a price and most have been paid. The country's highest honour belongs to a cat food firm.
after.muddle: The price list was banned and kept, and honours are still bought, though now through a very discreet broker.
after.ascent: The sale of honours ended the list for good. The country honours people now by naming bus shelters after them, for free.

after.decay: The lease on the port ran out and was renewed by the line, which by then owned the government that renewed it.
after.muddle: The port stayed leased for its ninety-nine years, and the country paid its fees for all of them.
after.ascent: The lease was broken in court, and the harbour was run in the open from then on. The line keeps one berth.

after.decay: You lost the office and won it back at the next count, honestly. Then you did nothing different with it.
after.muddle: You lost the office and won it back honestly. The country learned it could do that, and did it often.
after.ascent: You lost the office and won it back honestly, and the second term is the one they wrote about.

after.decay: You lost the office at a count and went. What came after was worse, and you watched it from across the chamber.
after.muddle: You lost the office at a count and went quietly, which was new, and did not last.
after.ascent: You lost the office at a count and went. The country remembers, above everything else, that you went.
